Survivalist es un juego de rol y supervivencia en mundo abierto ambientado tras un colapso global. Encarnas a un superviviente que emerge de su refugio para descubrir un mundo transformado, donde los recursos son escasos, los peligros constantes y cada decisión tiene consecuencias reales.

Tu misión es explorar, reunir suministros, construir una base funcional y establecer relaciones con otros supervivientes. El sistema social es uno de los pilares del juego: podrás reclutar aliados, negociar, colaborar o enfrentarte a otros grupos, influyendo directamente en el desarrollo de tu comunidad y en el rumbo de la historia.

Con un enfoque estratégico y libertad total para afrontar los desafíos, Survivalist combina gestión, exploración y narrativa emergente para ofrecer una experiencia de supervivencia profunda y rejugable.

Pros: 

Mundo abierto dinámico: Libertad total para explorar, gestionar recursos y decidir tu propio camino.
Sistema social profundo: Las relaciones con otros supervivientes influyen de forma real en la historia y en tu comunidad.
Alta rejugabilidad: Cada partida puede desarrollarse de forma distinta según tus decisiones y los grupos que encuentres.
Gestión estratégica: Construcción de bases, reclutamiento, comercio y toma de decisiones que afectan a largo plazo.
Narrativa emergente: Las situaciones que surgen de forma espontánea crean historias únicas en cada sesión.

Contras
Apartado visual modesto: Gráficos funcionales pero lejos de los estándares actuales del género.
Curva de aprendizaje pronunciada: Puede resultar abrumador al principio por la cantidad de sistemas y micromecánicas.
Interfaz algo tosca: Algunos menús y controles pueden sentirse poco intuitivos.
Ritmo irregular: Hay momentos muy intensos y otros más lentos.
IA variable: Comportamientos de aliados y enemigos que a veces pueden resultar impredecibles.

Survivalist is one of those hidden indie gems that punches way above its weight. It may not look like much at first glance, but under the hood, it’s got a surprisingly rich blend of survival mechanics, character interaction, and RPG progression. It’s a bit janky, sure—but also pretty addicting.

Gameplay mechanics are deeper than you'd expect. You scavenge for resources, recruit survivors, manage relationships, and build up your base. Combat is functional, if a little stiff, but it’s the systems interacting—hunger, trust, loyalty, skills—that really drive the gameplay. Score: 7/10.

Narrative is lightly structured. You start with a backstory and there are quests and dialogue trees with different outcomes, but it’s not a tightly written plot. The story emerges more through choices and how your community develops. Score: 6/10.

Graphics are very dated, even for its release window. Simple models, stiff animations, and an overall “budget indie” look are part of the package. That said, it’s easy to read, and eventually, you stop noticing. Score: 5/10.

Sound and music are nothing special. Basic effects and minimal background music do the job, but they’re clearly not the focus here. Score: 5/10.

Replayability is solid. Each playthrough can vary depending on who you meet, who you recruit, and how you handle events. The sandbox structure gives you a reason to try different strategies. Score: 7/10.

Innovation deserves some credit. It mixes survival, base-building, and social sim elements in a way that feels unique—especially given the small dev team. Score: 7/10.

Bottom line: Survivalist is rough around the edges but has real heart. If you're into systems-driven survival games with a bit of roleplaying and aren't scared off by dated visuals, it’s definitely worth a shot.

Survivalist – More Surviving, Less Thriving 🏚️🚫

Survivalist promises an open-world RPG with freedom and consequences, but what you get is a world that's more frustrating than it is immersive. After the collapse of civilization, you step into the shoes of Joe Wheeler, a hedge fund manager who somehow survived in his fancy bunker while the world crumbled. The game kicks off with high hopes but quickly plummets into a sluggish mess of awkward mechanics and a world that feels empty rather than expansive. 😩🌍

The freedom to play how you want sounds great in theory, but it’s often bogged down by clunky controls and bizarre interactions. Your choices may have consequences, but those consequences mostly result in confusing story paths or frustrating encounters that don't feel rewarding. There’s a ton of potential for survival and exploration here, but it’s buried under layers of frustration, weird pacing, and unintuitive gameplay. 🕹️💥

At the end of the day, Survivalist doesn’t feel like a post-apocalyptic adventure; it feels more like a chore. If you’re looking for a gripping RPG with meaningful choices and exploration, this one might leave you wishing you’d stayed in your bunker. 😔💀

This is a good post-apocalyptic zombie survival builder game.  You'll meet lots of characters with different personalities, and many of them will have backstories to delve into.  Most of them will belong to various good, neutral, or evil factions.  There's also an overall story to the game,

Meet new people, and try to recruit them to follow you.  Scavenge for new supplies, and build your own little survivor compound.  Choose to either try to get along with the other factions you come across, or try to conquer them.  Defend you and your group against bandits and raiders.  Barter when you can.  And for maximum entertainment, blow up buildings.

I'm not really a fan of the top-down camera, and waiting for your people to complete tasks, like Isham collecting wood planks to build stuff with, can be very tedious.  If you take the diabetic Alice into your group, then constantly needing to find her some insulin can also be a grind.  It makes for a good challenge, yes, but it's still a grind. Some of the zombies are slow, and some are real speedsters.  I don't like the speedsters, as they often come racing into view from nowhere.  They cover the distance between them and me so fast that I don't have time to respond, especially if there's more than one of them.  Lastly, I find the controls a little clunky.  Overall though, this game is definitely worth the 99 cents I paid for it.

One word to describe it, clunky. 

Absolutely do not bother. 

It's a one-dev game, and sadly, it is painfully apparent. The UI plus many systems in the game render it a frustrating experience. They don't lift up the game or make it more interesting - they just drag it down. Survivalist feels more like work than a game.

While the game has its challenges, it lacks depth and quickly becomes monotonous. The lack of stealth mechanics plys zombies detecting you before you see them, makes avoidance almost impossible at times. The shooting mechanics are equally problematic; guns are wildly inaccurate even at close range, making it difficult to hit targets. Given the high health of zombies, you'll expend several clips just to take one down. While there's an overabundance of ammunition, it undermines the realism and tension of scavenging for supplies. A better balance would be to improve gun accuracy and reduce ammo availability, creating a more authentic post-apocalyptic experience. As it stands, it feels like the entire map was very recently used as an ammo dump, flush with whatever your gun's receiver may require.

Another significant issue is the limited inventory size. Without backpacks, characters can carry very few items, making scavenging runs inefficient. Ammo alone takes up simply too much space, even when carrying just enough to handle a few zombies. The backpack system exacerbates the problem, as backpacks are hard to find, leaving you underprepared for extended periods. This makes it challenging to gather food and medicine quickly, and you can't begin constructing shelters until you locate a backpack, further hindering progress.

Survivalist's narrative attempts are, unfortunately, outdated. The dialogue options are overly formulaic, with a fixed list of questions yielding mostly identical responses from every character. This rigid execution strips the conversations of any emotional depth, making the interactions feel shallow and repetitive.

Yes, of course, there are positives, but the downsides and cons are significant and noteworthy enough that I felt this review should focus on that. After all, my review is a thumbs down and I aim to save you your money.

Sure, I know, it's only $5 USD, but it's a game I gave up on more quickly than expected and have no intention of ever playing it again. I constantly grappled with a poor user interface and flawed follower AI. Most of my time was spent running back and forth across the map, transporting a single item or two at a time. I can't recommend anyone bother with it. If you already have it in your library, just filter it out and move on. It's not worth your time.

Good for its time (I still remember seeing this on the XBLA Indie Game section!) but imo it didn't age well. Controls are frustrating, you often fight with the camera angle, and the story setup doesn't feel right (you get thousands of rounds of ammo and plenty of food, water, and base materials all on day 1). For me the difficulty comes from the bullet sponge zombies and cracked raider AI, or the constant insulin fetch quest that reminds me of the Zombrex you had to repeatedly retrieve over the course of Dead Rising 2. 

The main appeal seems to be the base building, and how you can control each of your community members and give them different tasks, in contrast to State of Decay where you yourself had to do most of the work/scavenging. I can see how this could be fun as a sort of XBLA colony-sim meets isometric rpg with survival elements, but it just didn't click for me.

The price is unbeatable however, and if the prior description sounds interesting to you then you should definitely give this game a shot! Just get ready to be in it for the long haul. Thumbs up since at its core this is a solid game that the dev cares for. It just isn't for me.
